notes.text:
The application shell loads Bootstrap 3.3.7 CSS from `maxcdn.bootstrapcdn.com` without an `integrity` attribute:

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://maxcdn.bootstrapcdn.com/bootstrap/3.3.7/css/bootstrap.min.css">
...
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://maxcdn.bootstrapcdn.com/bootstrap/3.3.7/css/bootstrap-theme.min.css">
```

Without Subresource Integrity the browser will apply whatever content the CDN (or an on-path attacker who can terminate TLS for that hostname) returns. Because these are stylesheets rather than scripts, the ceiling is CSS injection: UI redressing/defacement, form-overlay phishing within the DCE dashboard, or limited data exfiltration via CSS attribute selectors — not arbitrary JavaScript execution. These are the only two external resource loads in the repository (`index.html` is the sole HTML file; a repository-wide grep finds no other external `<link>` or `<script>` reference in first-party code).

Line 14 of the same file contains a **commented-out** `<script src="https://cdn.polyfill.io/v2/polyfill.min.js">` tag. `polyfill.io` was sold in 2024 and subsequently served malicious JavaScript to downstream sites. Because the tag is inside an HTML comment it is inert and is **not** filed as a finding; it is noted here so that it is not accidentally re-enabled.

cwe.name: Use of Unmaintained Third Party Components

notes.text:
The repository declares 38 devDependencies and 41 runtime dependencies pinned to 2016-2017 versions and commits no `package-lock.json` or `yarn.lock`. As a result, every software-composition-analysis tool run during this review (npm-audit, osv-scanner, trivy, grype) returned zero results — not because the dependency tree is clean, but because no resolved tree exists to scan (`npm-audit` reported `ENOLOCK`; `osv-scanner` reported "No package sources found").

Exact-pinned devDependencies with published advisories include:

| Package | Pin | Advisory | Effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| `webpack-dev-server` | `1.14.1` | CVE-2018-14732 | Missing WebSocket origin check — a malicious website can read the developer's source code while `npm start` is running |
| `cross-spawn` | `4.0.0` | CVE-2024-21538 | Regular-expression denial of service |
| `url-loader` | `0.5.7` | GHSA (via `mime` <1.4.1) | ReDoS |
| `eslint` | `3.1.1` | multiple transitive | — |
| `html-webpack-plugin` | `2.22.0` | lodash prototype-pollution transitives | — |
| `gulp` / `gulp-util` | `^3.9.1` / `^3.0.8` | deprecated; lodash/minimatch transitives | — |

All of the above are **build/development toolchain** packages; none ship in the production browser bundle. Runtime dependencies (`jquery ^3.1.1`, `bootstrap ^3.3.7`, `react ^15.6.1`, etc.) use caret ranges and would resolve above most known-vulnerable versions on a fresh install today, but without a committed lockfile the actually-deployed composition in 2018 is unverifiable.

Additional affected files (entire file): package.json

cwe.name: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

notes.text:
The gulp build script hardcodes the internal SSA SMB/UNC share used as the development deployment target:

```js
var devDest = '//ba/esefdata/EDIMA/DCE/Apps/DCE-Dashboard/DCE-UI'
```

This discloses an internal SSA file-server hostname (`ba`), an SMB share name (`esefdata`), and the internal directory hierarchy (`EDIMA/DCE/Apps/DCE-Dashboard/DCE-UI`). The repository was otherwise sanitised before publication — `src/components/Header.js` and `README.md` contain literal `[SERVER_NAME]` and `[EMAIL_ADDRESS]` placeholders — but the sanitisation pass missed `gulpfile.js`. The `cleanDevDest` (line 21) and `copyBuild` (line 28) tasks in the same file operate directly on this path.
